By the time I finished, I had worked in that building for thirty-one years.
I had been arriving home at ten for so long that nine felt like an afternoon.
Nobody had told me that the first month would be the hardest.
I had never had a free Tuesday before, and I did not know what to do with it.
How long had you been at that company when you decided to stop?
By the time I finished, thirty-one years. And I had been telling myself for most of them that the hours were temporary.
They never are. Mine were twenty-four years, and the first six months afterwards were the hardest part of the whole thing.
Harder than the last day? I had expected the last day to be the difficult one.
The last day is a party. Nobody had warned me about the Tuesdays.
And what changed after those six months?
I stopped trying to fill the time and started choosing what to put in it. It sounds like the same sentence. It is not.
In hindsight I had been ready for two years before I admitted it. I just had not said it out loud.
By the time I stopped, I had been in the same building for thirty-one years.
Nobody had warned me about the Tuesdays.
In hindsight I had been ready for two years before I admitted it.
It was bittersweet, and I would not change the people.
I am still building the new routine, and that is the honest answer.

Thank you. I will keep this to two minutes, which is about a minute and a half longer than anybody wants after dinner. When I started here I was twenty-six, and I had already been told by two people that the job would not last. By the time I finished, I had worked in this building for thirty-one years, under four presidents, and I had moved offices nine times without ever moving floor. What I want to say is this. For most of those years I had been arriving home at ten at night, and I had told myself it was temporary, and it was not. I am not going to pretend I would do it all again the same way. But I would do most of it, and I would do it with the same people, which is the part nobody writes into a career plan. Thank you for that.

When people tell the story of their own life in a second language, they almost always produce a list. I did this, then I did that, then I moved here. The list is accurate and nobody listens to it, including the person telling it. Here is what changes it, and it is one grammatical move. Put one thing behind another. Instead of I worked there for thirty years and then I retired, say by the time I retired I had been working in the same building for thirty years. Suddenly there is a shape, because the listener can hear which event is the frame and which one is the background. English does this constantly and speakers of other languages often do not, and it is the single clearest difference between a story and a list. One more thing. You do not need many of these. Two in a two minute story is plenty. What you are buying is not decoration, it is depth.
